newsitem.title: FRANCE: Total in LPG joint ventures in China.
newsitem.headline: Total in LPG joint ventures in China.

text.p: French oil company Total SA said on Wednesday it had entered the Chinese liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) market with the recent signing of two joint-venture agreements in the Shandong and Canton provinces.
In Shandong, 500 km from Beijing, Total has acquired a 35 percent stake in a project for the reception, storage and bulk sale of LPG and liquid chemicals.
The deal provides for the construction of a port receiving terminal and a depot. It said the total project represents a $12 million investment.
Total said it had also set up a company with two Japanese partners to acquire a 50 percent interest in a LPG storage and distribution joint venture in Shenzhen in Canton province.

"The partnerships, together with the initial agreements entered into in Vietnam and India, have strengthened Total's position in the rapidly emerging LPG market in the heart of a region where demand for energy is growing at an exceptional rate," Total said.
